name.en: Advanced English for Industry Professionals I

description.zh: 本課程將從整體產業概況出發，引導學生了解該產業的發展脈絡、市場動態等，並探討產業內的核心專業術語與表達方式。本課程旨在引導學生深入探索特定產業領域的英語應用，使其不僅能掌握專業術語，更能靈活運用於實際職場情境中。學生將逐步提升閱讀、寫作、聽力及口語表達能力，並培養跨文化溝通的敏銳度，以期在未來的國際職場中，自信且流暢地運用英語進行專業交流。
description.en: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the specific industry, starting with an overview of the industry's landscape, including its development history and market dynamics. It will also delve into the core professional terminology and expressions used within the industry. The primary goal is to guide students in applying English effectively within their chosen industry, ensuring they not only grasp the technical vocabulary but can also utilize it confidently in real-world professional contexts. Students will progressively enhance their reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills, while also developing a keen awareness of cross-cultural communication. This will enable them to engage in professional exchanges confidently and fluently in future international workplaces.

name.en: Advanced English for Academic Oral Reports and Presentations I

description.zh: 本課程旨在進一步提升學生於學術會議與研討場合中以英語進行口頭報告、簡報發表及互動應對之能力。課程聚焦學術會議常見之發表形式，包括論文口頭發表、海報發表、研究摘要說明、短講及問答交流，並著重學術口語論述之組織、研究重點之清楚傳達、論點整合、聽眾互動與現場應答技巧。透過會議情境模擬、口頭報告、海報發表演練與回應活動，學生將強化其學術英語口語表達、簡報呈現與會議溝通能力，並建立參與國際學術交流之實務基礎。
description.en: This course aims to further develop students’ ability to deliver oral reports, conference presentations, and academic briefings in English in conference and seminar settings. It focuses on common forms of academic conference communication, including paper presentations, poster sessions, research summaries, short talks, and question-and-answer exchanges. Special emphasis is placed on organizing academic oral discourse, presenting research clearly, integrating key arguments, engaging with audiences, and responding effectively in live academic settings. Through conference simulations, oral presentation practice, poster presentation tasks, and response activities, students will strengthen their spoken academic English, presentation delivery, and conference communication skills, building a practical foundation for participation in international academic events.

description.en: This course is designed for students who are interested in improving English skills in the field of information technology. It aims to increase students’ reading fluency and improve their speaking skills needed to function and succeed in classroom settings and in future career. syllabi.outline:
本課程提供學生及職前專業人士必備之英語文語言技巧，強調工程專業領域之英文溝通能力之訓練。課程內容依學院專業內容區分並整合英語文之聽說讀寫之能力為未來全球化移動及以英語專業溝通人才培育為目標。
This course aims to provide pre-service engineering students/professionals with the adequate skills of the English language and communicative competence to facilitate their current academic and future career pursuits. Students are encouraged to utilize their domain expertise to participate in professional communication in English. Centered on the training of professional use of the English language, the ESP curriculum as the crux of a highly-integrated work of domain knowledge and the English learning development embodies the indispensable credentials required for a global profession.
syllabi.assessment:
Attendance and participation: 20%. Students are expected to attend class regularly and participate actively in pair work, group discussion, textbook activities, BESTEP-style tasks, and speaking practice.

Vocabulary, reading, listening, and in-class exercises: 25%. Students will complete textbook-based vocabulary exercises, reading and listening tasks, grammar practice, and visual-information activities involving tables, charts, graphs, and diagrams.

Homework and preparation: 20%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, listening notes, data description practice, short recordings, paragraph writing, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 15%. The midterm assessment will be based on Units 1–3 and may include reading comprehension, technology-related vocabulary, numerical data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 20%. The final assessment may include a short presentation and a written response based on an information technology topic. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, appropriate use of technology-related vocabulary, and ability to explain textual and visual information.

內容 Content: 第17至18週安排學生完成「英文口說影片期末呈現」之彈性學習任務。學生以小組為單位，透過線上討論進行主題確認、資料整理、內容分工、英文講稿撰寫與口說排練，並製作 annotated outline 與完整 script。學生可運用AI工具輔助主題發想、英文修訂、口說練習與簡報內容優化，但須保留個人與小組的原創表達。教師將以遠距方式提供任務說明、範例、檢核表與必要回饋。

時數 Hours: 4

學習成果 Learning Outcomes: 學生須繳交英文口說影片、annotated outline 及完整 script。學習成效將依據內容組織、英文表達、口說流暢度、主題掌握、AI工具使用情形、團隊分工與影片完成度進行評量。

評量比例 Assessment Percentage: 25%

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to professional English for information and new technology; diagnostic speaking and writing activity.

Week 2: Unit 1 Big Data — Introduction to big data, data use, and technology-related vocabulary; discussion: What is big data and how do we use it?

Week 3: Unit 1 — Reading and listening practice on types of big data and their uses; speaking task: explaining one example of data use in daily life or industry.

Week 4: BESTEP skill focus — posters, flyers, and maps; summarizing and responding to visual information in English.

Week 5: Unit 2 Artificial Intelligence — Human, animal, and non-biological intelligence; reading and discussion on artificial intelligence.

Week 6: Unit 2 — Uses of AI; speaking task: discussing an AI-driven technology; writing task: describing the benefits and risks of an AI application.

Week 7: BESTEP skill focus — tables and numerical data; reporting common numbers, describing data, and comparing figures in English.

Week 8: Unit 3 Robotics — Robotics and improving human life; reading and discussion on the history and development of robotics.

Week 9: Midterm Exam Week — Midterm assessment based on Units 1–3 and BESTEP-related skills, including reading comprehension, vocabulary, data description, and a short speaking or writing task.

Week 10: Unit 3 — Advances in robotics; listening and speaking task: explaining the function of a programmable robot or robotic system.

Week 11: BESTEP skill focus — pie charts and bar charts; presenting survey results, describing proportions, and comparing responses from different groups.

Week 12: Unit 4 Hackers and Internet Security — Introduction to internet security, hackers, ransomware, and online safety.

Week 13: Unit 4 — Good and bad hackers; discussion and writing task: explaining a computer security problem and proposing possible solutions.

Week 14: Unit 5 Problem Solving — Identifying and solving problems; reading and discussion on facing uncertainties and making positive changes.

Week 15: BESTEP skill focus — flowcharts and process description; explaining a problem-solving process step by step.

Week 16: Unit 6 DNA Testing and Family History — DNA research, DNA testing, and personal information; discussion: How important is a person’s DNA?

Week 17: Unit 6 — A DNA test; writing workshop: explaining advantages, disadvantages, and ethical concerns related to DNA testing or personal data.

Week 18: Final assessment — short oral presentation and written response based on an information technology topic with one visual aid, such as a table, chart, graph, diagram, or flowchart; course reflection.

description.zh: 本課程將從整體產業概況出發，引導學生了解該產業的發展脈絡、市場動態等，並探討產業內的核心專業術語與表達方式。本課程旨在引導學生深入探索特定產業領域的英語應用，使其不僅能掌握專業術語，更能靈活運用於實際職場情境中。學生將逐步提升閱讀、寫作、聽力及口語表達能力，並培養跨文化溝通的敏銳度，以期在未來的國際職場中，自信且流暢地運用英語進行專業交流。
description.en: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the specific industry, starting with an overview of the industry's landscape, including its development history and market dynamics. It will also delve into the core professional terminology and expressions used within the industry. The primary goal is to guide students in applying English effectively within their chosen industry, ensuring they not only grasp the technical vocabulary but can also utilize it confidently in real-world professional contexts. Students will progressively enhance their reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills, while also developing a keen awareness of cross-cultural communication. This will enable them to engage in professional exchanges confidently and fluently in future international workplaces.

syllabi.outline: 課程重點：(1)藉由適合其程度的教材加強學生必備的基礎文法觀念和句型結構；(2)使學生確切把握閱讀要領以及充分瞭解寫作的各種技巧，重心在生字、片語、句法的解釋和基本寫作技巧的分析；(3)熟悉英語人士日常生活情境及與學生將來就業環境相關之會話及適當之應對方式；(4)透過練習加強聽、說、讀、寫的知能及表達。

name.en: Advanced English for Academic Oral Reports and Presentations I

description.zh: 本課程旨在進一步提升學生於學術會議與研討場合中以英語進行口頭報告、簡報發表及互動應對之能力。課程聚焦學術會議常見之發表形式，包括論文口頭發表、海報發表、研究摘要說明、短講及問答交流，並著重學術口語論述之組織、研究重點之清楚傳達、論點整合、聽眾互動與現場應答技巧。透過會議情境模擬、口頭報告、海報發表演練與回應活動，學生將強化其學術英語口語表達、簡報呈現與會議溝通能力，並建立參與國際學術交流之實務基礎。
description.en: This course aims to further develop students’ ability to deliver oral reports, conference presentations, and academic briefings in English in conference and seminar settings. It focuses on common forms of academic conference communication, including paper presentations, poster sessions, research summaries, short talks, and question-and-answer exchanges. Special emphasis is placed on organizing academic oral discourse, presenting research clearly, integrating key arguments, engaging with audiences, and responding effectively in live academic settings. Through conference simulations, oral presentation practice, poster presentation tasks, and response activities, students will strengthen their spoken academic English, presentation delivery, and conference communication skills, building a practical foundation for participation in international academic events.

syllabi.assessment:
The final grade for this course consists of two parts: the institutional English proficiency exam, which accounts for 20% of the total grade, and instructor-based assessment, which accounts for 80%.

The instructor-based assessment emphasizes students’ continuous participation, in-class speaking practice, presentation preparation, group discussion, peer feedback, and learning process throughout the semester. Since this is a presentation-oriented course, many learning outcomes can only be demonstrated through in-class activities, oral practice, group tasks, and real-time feedback. Therefore, students who are absent from class will not be able to receive points for the in-class participation, speaking practice, group interaction, or presentation activities missed on that day.

The grading breakdown is as follows:

Institutional English Proficiency Exam: 20%

Class Participation and Coursework: 40%
This includes attendance, in-class participation, speaking practice, group discussion, presentation activities, classroom tasks, peer feedback, worksheets, online assignments, and staged preparation for presentations. This category places strong emphasis on sustained participation throughout the semester. Students who are absent may not make up points for in-class participation, oral practice, group interaction, or real-time classroom activities simply by submitting written assignments afterward.

Midterm Performance Assessment: 15%
This is a formative assessment based on the course progress. It may include presentation topic proposals, presentation outlines, slide structure, individual or group oral reports, draft presentations, peer feedback, and learning process checks. This course does not include an additional traditional written midterm exam; instead, midterm assessment is based on practical performance and staged learning outcomes.

Final Project Assessment: 25%
This includes the final English presentation or video presentation, slides, speaking notes or script, content organization, use of management-related professional English, oral delivery, visual design, time management, and reflection. If Weeks 17–18 are conducted as online flexible learning weeks, the final project may be completed through video presentation submission, online peer review, and individual reflection.

Additional note:

This course values the learning process and regular classroom engagement. Students who are frequently absent will have difficulty completing in-class speaking practice, group tasks, and formative assessments. Even if a student submits the final project, long-term absence may still significantly affect the final grade. Late or make-up assignments may only be counted for the written or file-submission component, depending on the nature of the task. They cannot replace attendance, real-time oral performance, peer interaction, or instructor-observed classroom performance.

Homework and preparation: 16%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, data description practice, writing tasks, short recordings, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 12%. The midterm assessment will be based on the first half of the semester and may include vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 16%. The final assessment may include a short presentation, written response, reading task, vocabulary review, or integrated textual and visual information task. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, content understanding, and appropriate use of course-related English.

University English proficiency exam: 20%

The university English proficiency exam accounts for 20% of the final grade. Students are required to follow the university’s official regulations and schedule for this exam.

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
Week 1 | Course Orientation and Introduction to Management Presentations | Introduce the course plan, grading policy, group arrangements, and AI-use guidelines; complete a short self-introduction and diagnostic speaking task.

Week 2 | Teaching Practice Module: Pre-test and Introduction to Screening Ideas | Complete the pre-test, build a group vocabulary bank, and learn key concepts such as screening ideas, criteria, and feasibility.

Week 3 | Screening Ideas and Decision-Making | Practice comparing options, explaining reasons, and making decisions; complete a group idea-screening task and a 2-minute briefing.

Week 4 | Creative Script Writing #1 | Complete the first management-scenario script draft, conduct peer feedback, and give a short oral explanation.

Week 5 | Innovation and Product Proposal | Learn vocabulary related to innovation and new product development; design a creative product or service scenario.

Week 6 | Creative Script Writing #2 and Revision | Complete the second script, revise language and vocabulary use, and practice turning dialogue into presentation content.

Week 7 | Impromptu Writing / Speaking and Post-test | Complete an impromptu writing or speaking task, take the post-test, and complete the learning questionnaire.

Week 8 | From Script to Presentation | Organize the work from Weeks 2–7 and turn the scripts and discussions into a group presentation outline.

Week 9 | Midterm Exam Week and Presentation Outline Check | Follow the institutional midterm English exam schedule; no additional written midterm exam will be given for this course; check presentation topics and outlines.

Week 10 | Feasibility Study and Presentation Structure | Learn expressions related to feasibility studies and practice problem-solution presentation structure through a group mini presentation.

Week 11 | Marketing Principles and Audience Awareness | Learn concepts such as target customers, needs, and wants; practice designing presentation content for a specific audience.

Week 12 | Marketing Planning and SWOT | Practice explaining SWOT analysis in English and complete one group SWOT slide.

Week 13 | Marketing Mix and Product Life Cycle | Learn the 4Ps/7Ps and product life cycle; practice using visual slides to explain product strategy.

Week 14 | Market Research and Data Commentary | Practice describing market research data, charts, and trends; complete a 2-minute data commentary.

Week 15 | Online Marketing and Digital Business | Analyze the online marketing strategy of a brand or platform and practice case-based English presentation.

Week 16 | Final Video Presentation Workshop | Explain the requirements for the final video presentation; complete the presentation outline, slide draft, and recording practice.

Week 17 | Online Flexible Learning: Final Video Presentation | Submit the final English video presentation, slides, and speaking notes or script online.

Week 18 | Online Flexible Learning: Peer Review and Reflection | Watch classmates’ video presentations, complete peer review, and submit an individual reflection and presentation portfolio.

description.zh: 本課程將從整體產業概況出發，引導學生了解該產業的發展脈絡、市場動態等，並探討產業內的核心專業術語與表達方式。本課程旨在引導學生深入探索特定產業領域的英語應用，使其不僅能掌握專業術語，更能靈活運用於實際職場情境中。學生將逐步提升閱讀、寫作、聽力及口語表達能力，並培養跨文化溝通的敏銳度，以期在未來的國際職場中，自信且流暢地運用英語進行專業交流。
description.en: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the specific industry, starting with an overview of the industry's landscape, including its development history and market dynamics. It will also delve into the core professional terminology and expressions used within the industry. The primary goal is to guide students in applying English effectively within their chosen industry, ensuring they not only grasp the technical vocabulary but can also utilize it confidently in real-world professional contexts. Students will progressively enhance their reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills, while also developing a keen awareness of cross-cultural communication. This will enable them to engage in professional exchanges confidently and fluently in future international workplaces.

description.zh: 本課程教授科技及商業領域知識以及實務應用。修習本課程之學生，將習得中高階英語素養以及科技與商務溝通基本知識。課程內容包含: 基礎科技及商業概念、重點時事科技及商業議題、基本科技及商業字彙，和廣泛科技及商業實務用語。
description.en: This course teaches knowledge and practical applications in the fields of technology and business. Students taking this course will acquire intermediate to upper-intermediate English proficiency and basic knowledge of technology and business communication. The course content includes: fundamental technology and business concepts, key current technology and business issues, basic technology and business vocabulary, and a wide range of practical technology and business terminology.

syllabi.outline:
本課程教授科技及商業領域知識以及實務應用。修習本課程之學生，將習得中高階英語素養以及科技與商務溝通基本知識。課程內容包含: 基礎科技及商業概念、重點時事科技及商業議題、基本科技及商業字彙，和廣泛科技及商業實務用語。
This course teaches knowledge and practical applications in the fields of technology and business. Students taking this course will acquire intermediate to upper-intermediate English proficiency and basic knowledge of technology and business communication. The course content includes: fundamental technology and business concepts, key current technology and business issues, basic technology and business vocabulary, and a wide range of practical technology and business terminology.

name.zh: 商業英文會議與簡報(一)
name.en: English for Business Meetings and Presentations I

description.zh: 本課程旨在培養學生在商務情境中以英語參與會議與進行簡報的基礎能力。課程內容涵蓋會議常用語、簡報組織、意見表達、回應與提問等實用溝通技巧，幫助學生熟悉職場常見的英語溝通情境。透過情境對話、角色扮演、小組任務與簡短商務簡報等活動，學生將提升英語口語表達、自信與互動能力，並建立在商務會議與簡報場合中進行基本溝通的能力。
description.en: This course aims to develop their basic ability to participate in business meetings and give presentations in English. The course covers useful language and communication skills for workplace contexts, including meeting expressions, presentation organization, expressing opinions, responding to others, and asking questions. Through situational dialogues, role-plays, group tasks, and short business presentations, students will build confidence and improve their spoken English for effective communication in business meeting and presentation settings.

syllabi.outline:
本課程旨在提升學生資訊領域的英語文能力，加強學生於該領域課堂學習與未來職業所需的閱讀與口說技巧。本課程中，學生將經由研讀資訊領域相關文章以及針對相關主題的討論，增加資訊領域的字彙，並加強英語能力與溝通技巧。
This course is designed for students who are interested in improving English skills in the field of information technology. It aims to increase students’ reading fluency and improve their speaking skills needed to function and succeed in classroom settings and in future career. In this course, authentic reading texts related to information technology will be used. Students will discuss topics, such as artificial intelligence and the World Wide Web, in order to expand vocabulary and language skills.

description.zh: 本課程將從整體產業概況出發，引導學生了解該產業的發展脈絡、市場動態等，並探討產業內的核心專業術語與表達方式。本課程旨在引導學生深入探索特定產業領域的英語應用，使其不僅能掌握專業術語，更能靈活運用於實際職場情境中。學生將逐步提升閱讀、寫作、聽力及口語表達能力，並培養跨文化溝通的敏銳度，以期在未來的國際職場中，自信且流暢地運用英語進行專業交流。
description.en: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the specific industry, starting with an overview of the industry's landscape, including its development history and market dynamics. It will also delve into the core professional terminology and expressions used within the industry. The primary goal is to guide students in applying English effectively within their chosen industry, ensuring they not only grasp the technical vocabulary but can also utilize it confidently in real-world professional contexts. Students will progressively enhance their reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills, while also developing a keen awareness of cross-cultural communication. This will enable them to engage in professional exchanges confidently and fluently in future international workplaces.

description.zh: 本課程旨在幫助學生提升對全球永續發展目標（SDGs）及當前全球性議題的理解，並能夠用英文進行有效的溝通與表達。學生將學會如何以英文探討全球性問題，如貧窮、氣候變遷、性別平等等，並能在學術、專業及公共討論中自信地發表意見。
description.en: This course is designed for undergraduate students to develop their academic English language skills for success in English-medium university coursework. This course will engage students with active participation in a variety of academic listening, reading, writing, and speaking activities that they would encounter in real-life academic university lectures and professional workplace environments.

name.en: Advanced English for Popular Culture I

description.zh: 本課程旨在進一步提升學生以英語分析、比較與討論流行文化議題之能力，並深化其對當代文化產業與跨文化傳播的理解。課程內容涵蓋全球流行趨勢、影視與數位媒體、運動與娛樂文化、粉絲文化、名人與網紅現象、品牌與消費文化，以及青年文化與社群互動等主題，並探討流行文化與身分認同、媒體再現、商業化及全球文化流動之關聯。透過議題討論、案例分析、口頭報告、比較評論與主題簡報等活動，學生將提升英語分析與論述能力，並培養對流行文化現象之批判思考與跨文化視野。
description.en: This course further develops students’ ability to analyze, compare, and discuss issues in popular culture in English while deepening their understanding of contemporary cultural industries and cross-cultural communication. Topics include global popular trends, film and digital media, sports and entertainment culture, fan culture, celebrity and influence culture, branding and consumer culture, and youth culture in online and social spaces. Students will also explore the relationship between popular culture and identity, media representation, commercialization, and global cultural flows. Through issue-based discussion, case analysis, oral reports, comparative commentary, and thematic presentations, students will strengthen their English analytical and expressive abilities while developing critical perspectives on popular culture and its broader social and cultural impact.

syllabi.outline: In order to cultivate the students’ comprehensive capabilities to use English, especially the listening comprehension and oral expression ability, different multimedia materials in popular culture, including movies, songs, TV series, and animations, are used to help students understand when and how to use language appropriately in various situations. Different activities (listening practice, role-play, group discussion, and oral presentation) are designed to facilitate students’ English learning.

name.en: Advanced English for Industry Professionals I

description.zh: 本課程將從整體產業概況出發，引導學生了解該產業的發展脈絡、市場動態等，並探討產業內的核心專業術語與表達方式。本課程旨在引導學生深入探索特定產業領域的英語應用，使其不僅能掌握專業術語，更能靈活運用於實際職場情境中。學生將逐步提升閱讀、寫作、聽力及口語表達能力，並培養跨文化溝通的敏銳度，以期在未來的國際職場中，自信且流暢地運用英語進行專業交流。
description.en: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the specific industry, starting with an overview of the industry's landscape, including its development history and market dynamics. It will also delve into the core professional terminology and expressions used within the industry. The primary goal is to guide students in applying English effectively within their chosen industry, ensuring they not only grasp the technical vocabulary but can also utilize it confidently in real-world professional contexts. Students will progressively enhance their reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills, while also developing a keen awareness of cross-cultural communication. This will enable them to engage in professional exchanges confidently and fluently in future international workplaces.

description.zh: 本課程提供學生及職前專業人士必備之英語文語言技巧，強調設計與人文專業領域之英文溝通能力之訓練。課程內容依學院專業內容區分並整合英語文之聽說讀寫之能力為未來全球化移動及以英語專業溝通人才培育為目標。
description.en: This course aims to provide pre-service design and cultural business students/professionals with the adequate skills of the English language and communicative competence to facilitate their current academic and future career pursuits. Students are encouraged to utilize their domain expertise to participate in professional communication in English. Centered on the training of professional use of the English language, the ESP curriculum as the crux of a highly-integrated work of domain knowledge and the English learning development embodies the indispensable credentials required for a global profession.

syllabi.outline:
本課程培養學生提供在科技領域中使用英語的能力。 學生將獲得基本的英語語言技能、詞彙、結構和科技英語的風格。 此外，該課程還強調技術和工程領域的職場溝通能力。
The first part of the one-year / two-semester course aims to develop students’ basic English competence in the context of technology. Students are expected to acquire basic English language skills, vocabulary, structures and styles of technology English. In addition, the course also emphasizes workplace communication in the field of technology and engineering.

syllabi.notes:
【彈性教學週規劃】
第17週：期末口說評量採小組方式進行，各組依指定時段到課完成口頭報告與問答，未輪到之組別無須到課。課程時數3小時，依學生英語口語表達、溝通互動、發音、流暢度及內容組織等表現評分，占總成績10%。

第18週：期末寫作評量採線上數位學習方式進行。教師提供寫作教學影片，學生完成影片學習後依指定題目撰寫英文作文，並於期限內上傳至指定學習平台。課程時數3小時，依內容發展、組織結構、文法、字彙運用及整體表達能力評分，占總成績10%。

【課程說明】
未完整參與第一週課程者，不接受加選；加選條件及可加選人數依開課單位相關規定辦理。本課程使用生成式AI作為教學設計、教材製作及部分教學活動之輔助工具，並有條件允許學生於作業或報告中使用生成式AI，惟須簡要說明其用途。修讀本課程者視為已知悉並同意遵循本課程生成式AI使用規範。

syllabi.assessment:
The final grade for this course consists of two major parts: instructor-based assessment, which accounts for 80% of the final grade, and the university English proficiency exam, which accounts for 20% of the final grade.

Instructor-based assessment: 80%

Attendance and participation: 16%. Students are expected to attend class regularly and participate actively in pair work, group discussion, textbook activities, BESTEP-style tasks, and speaking practice.

Vocabulary, reading, and in-class exercises: 20%. Students will complete textbook-based vocabulary exercises, reading comprehension tasks, collocation practice, and activities involving textual and visual information such as tables, charts, graphs, diagrams, or short academic texts.

Homework and preparation: 16%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, data description practice, writing tasks, short recordings, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 12%. The midterm assessment will be based on the first half of the semester and may include vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 16%. The final assessment may include a short presentation, written response, reading task, vocabulary review, or integrated textual and visual information task. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, content understanding, and appropriate use of course-related English.

University English proficiency exam: 20%

The university English proficiency exam accounts for 20% of the final grade. Students are required to follow the university’s official regulations and schedule for this exam.

內容 Content: 第17至18週安排學生完成「英文口說影片期末呈現」之彈性學習任務。學生以小組為單位，透過線上討論進行主題確認、資料整理、內容分工、英文講稿撰寫與口說排練，並製作 annotated outline 與完整 script。學生可運用AI工具輔助主題發想、英文修訂、口說練習與簡報內容優化，但須保留個人與小組的原創表達。教師將以遠距方式提供任務說明、範例、檢核表與必要回饋。

時數 Hours: 6

學習成果 Learning Outcomes: 學生須繳交英文口說影片、annotated outline 及完整 script。學習成效將依據內容組織、英文表達、口說流暢度、主題掌握、AI工具使用情形、團隊分工與影片完成度進行評量。

評量比例 Assessment Percentage: 25%

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to professional English for mechanical and electrical engineering; diagnostic speaking and writing activity.

Week 2: Engineering drawings and design basics — drawings, views, scales, and design objectives; speaking task: explaining a simple product or machine design.

Week 3: BESTEP skill focus — posters, flyers, and maps; summarizing and responding to visual information in English.

Week 4: Measurements and numbers — horizontal and vertical measurements, dimensions, decimals, fractions, and basic calculations; writing task: describing measurements accurately.

Week 5: Area, size, mass, and measurable parameters — weight, mass, volume, density, input, output, efficiency, and capacity; speaking task: explaining numerical information.

Week 6: BESTEP skill focus — tables and numerical data; reporting common numbers and comparing data in English.

Week 7: Materials technology I — material types, metals, non-metals, steel, alloy steels, and corrosion; vocabulary and collocation practice.

Week 8: Materials technology II — polymers, minerals, ceramics, concrete, and wood; speaking task: comparing material properties and suitable applications.

Week 9: Midterm Exam Week — Midterm assessment based on Weeks 1–8, including technical vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short speaking or writing task.

Week 10: BESTEP skill focus — pie charts and bar charts; presenting survey results and describing part-to-whole relationships.

Week 11: Manufacturing and assembly I — 3D component features, machining, CNC, cutting tools, and high-temperature cutting techniques.

Week 12: Manufacturing and assembly II — mechanical fasteners, bolts, screws, washers, rivets, welding, brazing, soldering, and adhesives; writing task: describing assembly procedures.

Week 13: BESTEP skill focus — flowcharts and process description; explaining a technical or manufacturing process step by step.

Week 14: Static and dynamic principles — load, stress, strain, force, deformation, failure, motion, and simple machines.

Week 15: Mechanisms and energy — engines, motors, transmission, gears, work, power, energy efficiency, heat, and temperature.

Week 16: Electricity basics — current, voltage, resistance, electrical supply, circuits, and components; speaking task: explaining a basic electrical system.

Week 17: Integrated speaking and writing workshop — students prepare a short technical explanation using one visual aid, such as a table, graph, diagram, or flowchart.

Week 18: Final assessment — short oral presentation and written summary based on a mechanical/electrical engineering topic; course reflection.

內容 Content: 第17至18週安排學生完成「英文口說影片期末呈現」之彈性學習任務。學生以小組為單位，透過線上討論進行主題確認、資料整理、內容分工、英文講稿撰寫與口說排練，並製作 annotated outline 與完整 script。學生可運用AI工具輔助主題發想、英文修訂、口說練習與簡報內容優化，但須保留個人與小組的原創表達。教師將以遠距方式提供任務說明、範例、檢核表與必要回饋。

時數 Hours: 6

學習成果 Learning Outcomes: 學生須繳交英文口說影片、annotated outline 及完整 script。學習成效將依據內容組織、英文表達、口說流暢度、主題掌握、AI工具使用情形、團隊分工與影片完成度進行評量。

評量比例 Assessment Percentage: 25%

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to professional English for mechanical and electrical engineering; diagnostic speaking and writing activity.

Week 2: Engineering drawings and design basics — drawings, views, scales, and design objectives; speaking task: explaining a simple product or machine design.

Week 3: BESTEP skill focus — posters, flyers, and maps; summarizing and responding to visual information in English.

Week 4: Measurements and numbers — horizontal and vertical measurements, dimensions, decimals, fractions, and basic calculations; writing task: describing measurements accurately.

Week 5: Area, size, mass, and measurable parameters — weight, mass, volume, density, input, output, efficiency, and capacity; speaking task: explaining numerical information.

Week 6: BESTEP skill focus — tables and numerical data; reporting common numbers and comparing data in English.

Week 7: Materials technology I — material types, metals, non-metals, steel, alloy steels, and corrosion; vocabulary and collocation practice.

Week 8: Materials technology II — polymers, minerals, ceramics, concrete, and wood; speaking task: comparing material properties and suitable applications.

Week 9: Midterm Exam Week — Midterm assessment based on Weeks 1–8, including technical vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short speaking or writing task.

Week 10: BESTEP skill focus — pie charts and bar charts; presenting survey results and describing part-to-whole relationships.

Week 11: Manufacturing and assembly I — 3D component features, machining, CNC, cutting tools, and high-temperature cutting techniques.

Week 12: Manufacturing and assembly II — mechanical fasteners, bolts, screws, washers, rivets, welding, brazing, soldering, and adhesives; writing task: describing assembly procedures.

Week 13: BESTEP skill focus — flowcharts and process description; explaining a technical or manufacturing process step by step.

Week 14: Static and dynamic principles — load, stress, strain, force, deformation, failure, motion, and simple machines.

Week 15: Mechanisms and energy — engines, motors, transmission, gears, work, power, energy efficiency, heat, and temperature.

Week 16: Electricity basics — current, voltage, resistance, electrical supply, circuits, and components; speaking task: explaining a basic electrical system.

Week 17: Integrated speaking and writing workshop — students prepare a short technical explanation using one visual aid, such as a table, graph, diagram, or flowchart.

Week 18: Final assessment — short oral presentation and written summary based on a mechanical/electrical engineering topic; course reflection.

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
Week 1: Course Introduction & Cross-cultural Communication Warm-up 課程介紹、學習策略、跨文化溝通基礎、發音暖身與英語遊戲
Week 2: Introducing Yourself & Exchanging Personal Details 自我介紹、字母拼讀、基數與電話號碼
Week 3: Talking about Dates, Times & Schedules 日期、時間、序數、時刻表閱讀與聽力
Week 4: Identifying Objects & Technical Parts 零件與工具名稱、this/that/these/those、基本物件描述 
Week 5: Describing Size, Color & Quantity 尺寸、顏色、數量表達；物件描述對話練習
Week 6: Tools and Their Functions 工具部位、用途描述、have 句型與現在簡單式
Week 7: Positions, Locations & Occupations 位置介系詞、職業介紹、工作場域對話
Week 8: Listening/Reading Practice 聽力與閱讀技巧整合練習
Week 9: Midterm Exam 期中筆試
Week 10: Describing Movement & Direction 方向副詞、can / can't 表達能力、移動描述
Week 11: Controls, Speed & Operating Instructions 控制裝置、速度單位、imperative + present simple
Week 12: Fluid Systems & Flow 流體系統、進出方向介系詞、流動動詞
Week 13: Circuits & Cause-Effect Relationships 電路詞彙、電學單位、零條件句（If... , ...）
Week 14: Describing Ongoing Actions & Processes 現在進行式、動作描述、拼字規則
Week 15: Materials, Properties & Professional Contact Information 材料屬性、Email/網址唸法、電話應對句型
Week 16: Final Exam 期末筆試

(課程依照學生實際狀況微調)

syllabi.assessment:
The final grade for this course consists of two major parts: instructor-based assessment, which accounts for 80% of the final grade, and the university English proficiency exam, which accounts for 20% of the final grade.

Instructor-based assessment: 80%

Attendance and participation: 16%. Students are expected to attend class regularly and participate actively in pair work, group discussion, textbook activities, BESTEP-style tasks, and speaking practice.

Vocabulary, reading, and in-class exercises: 20%. Students will complete textbook-based vocabulary exercises, reading comprehension tasks, collocation practice, and activities involving textual and visual information such as tables, charts, graphs, diagrams, or short academic texts.

Homework and preparation: 16%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, data description practice, writing tasks, short recordings, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 12%. The midterm assessment will be based on the first half of the semester and may include vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 16%. The final assessment may include a short presentation, written response, reading task, vocabulary review, or integrated textual and visual information task. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, content understanding, and appropriate use of course-related English.

University English proficiency exam: 20%

The university English proficiency exam accounts for 20% of the final grade. Students are required to follow the university’s official regulations and schedule for this exam.

內容 Content: 第17至18週安排學生完成「英文口說影片期末呈現」之彈性學習任務。學生以小組為單位，透過線上討論進行主題確認、資料整理、內容分工、英文講稿撰寫與口說排練，並製作 annotated outline 與完整 script。學生可運用AI工具輔助主題發想、英文修訂、口說練習與簡報內容優化，但須保留個人與小組的原創表達。教師將以遠距方式提供任務說明、範例、檢核表與必要回饋。

時數 Hours: 6

學習成果 Learning Outcomes: 學生須繳交英文口說影片、annotated outline 及完整 script。學習成效將依據內容組織、英文表達、口說流暢度、主題掌握、AI工具使用情形、團隊分工與影片完成度進行評量。

評量比例 Assessment Percentage: 25%

extra.課程進度(1-16週):
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to professional English for engineering; diagnostic reading, speaking, and writing activity.

Week 2: Engineering design basics — drawings, design development, design objectives, and design solutions; speaking task: explaining a simple engineering design.

Week 3: BESTEP skill focus — posters, flyers, and maps; summarizing and responding to visual information in English.

Week 4: Measurement and dimensions — horizontal and vertical measurements, locating and setting out, dimensions of circles, and dimensional accuracy.

Week 5: Numbers and calculations — decimals, fractions, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, area, size, mass, volume, density, and measurable parameters.

Week 6: BESTEP skill focus — tables and numerical data; reporting numbers, comparing data, and describing engineering-related figures.

Week 7: Materials technology I — material types, metals, non-metals, steel, non-ferrous metals, polymers, minerals, and ceramics.

Week 8: Materials technology II — concrete, reinforced concrete, wood, tensile strength, deformation, hardness, fatigue, fracture toughness, and thermal properties.

Week 9: Midterm Exam Week — Midterm assessment based on Weeks 1–8, including technical vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short speaking or writing task.

Week 10: BESTEP skill focus — pie charts and bar charts; presenting survey results, describing proportions, and comparing responses from different groups.

Week 11: Forming and processing materials — casting, sintering, extruding, heat-treating metal, raw materials for processing, and formats of processed materials.

Week 12: Static and dynamic principles I — load, stress, strain, force, deformation, failure, and structural mechanics.

Week 13: BESTEP skill focus — line graphs; analyzing changes over time and predicting future trends in engineering or environmental data.

Week 14: Static and dynamic principles II — motion, simple machines, angular motion, rotary and reciprocating motion, engine revolutions, and friction.

Week 15: Energy and temperature — forms of energy, energy efficiency, work, power, changes of temperature and state, and heat transfer.

Week 16: Fluids — fluid containment, pipes, ducts, hoses, tanks, pumps, fans, turbines, fluid pressure, and fluid dynamics.

Week 17: BESTEP integrated academic English practice — summarizing the main points of a short academic text and integrating textual and graphical input.

Week 18: Final assessment — short oral presentation and written summary based on an engineering topic with one visual aid, such as a table, chart, graph, diagram, or flowchart; course reflection.

This course is for students, researchers, and practitioners who design or evaluate products for their target user. It covers evaluation methodology for supporting human factor design for products, human-machine systems, software applications, games, and specialized appliances intended to be used by people. This field contains a substantial body of knowledge with regard to human factor design and the more narrowly scoped field of usability engineering (UE). Within these areas of practice, and the related research field of HCI, a host of methods are available for evaluating interactive products for user. This course provides an overview of a new and vibrant research field and exposes gaps in current methodologies that future research must address. We also hope it conveys our enthusiasm for this research area, where so much interesting work is taking place and so much still needs to be done.

description.zh: 本課程以國際時事為主軸，培養學生於英語口語互動中之理解、回應、分析與論述能力。藉由課堂討論、小組對話、議題回應、立場表述及簡短口頭報告等活動，學生將學習從多元角度理解國際事件，整理資訊、辨識觀點，並以清楚且具邏輯的英語參與討論。課程亦著重培養批判思考與國際視野，以提升學生在全球議題脈絡中之英語溝通能力。
description.en: This course centers on international current affairs and aims to develop students’ ability to comprehend, respond to, analyze, and articulate ideas in spoken English interaction. Through class discussion, small-group dialogue, issue-based responses, position statements, and short oral presentations, students will learn to approach international events from multiple perspectives, organize information, identify viewpoints, and participate in discussion in clear and logical English. The course also emphasizes the development of critical thinking and global awareness in order to strengthen students’ English communication skills in the context of global issues.

description.zh: 本課程以主題式口語互動為核心，培養學生在英語交流中進行有內容、具結構性且能持續延伸之口語表達能力。課程著重於學生就特定主題或議題進行意見表達、回應、追問、延伸與整合，並學習在互動中有條理地組織想法、連結觀點及建構較完整的口語交流。透過配對對話、小組討論、主題回應與短篇口語任務等活動，學生將提升其英語口語互動、自主表達與持續性溝通能力，並為後續專業領域英語簡報課程奠定基礎。
description.en: This course focuses on thematic spoken interaction and aims to develop students’ ability to engage in meaningful, structured, and sustained communication in English. Rather than emphasizing everyday conversation or formal presentation, the course trains students to express ideas, respond to others, ask follow-up questions, extend discussion, and connect viewpoints around a topic or theme. Through pair interaction, small-group discussion, topic-based response tasks, and short speaking activities, students will learn to organize ideas more clearly and participate in more coherent and extended spoken exchanges in English. syllabi.outline:
什麼是人體結構和功能？
人體結構與功能是一門非必修主要課程，旨在探索人體形式和功能之間的基本關係。解剖學和生理學是生命科學中兩個最基本的術語和研究領域。解剖學是指身體的內部和外部結構及其物理關係，而生理學是指研究這些結構的功能。本課程旨在定義瞭解剖學和生理學，並解釋了為什麼它們對生物醫學工程很重要。主要器官系統的解剖學和生理學將在正常和疾病狀態的背景下進行研究。學生將學習關鍵的生物過程，如中心教條，膜擴散和運輸，細胞信號傳導，氣體交換，血流，營養吸收，血液pH平衡以及動作電位的產生和傳播。然後，學生將應用這些知識來瞭解器官如何對維持體內平衡的各種輸入做出反應。

課程將納入實踐演示，為課程中提供的資訊提供實用框架：
1.根據位置，功能，關鍵成分和解剖命名法確定主要的人體系統。  
2.展示對代謝功能和每個主要器官系統的生理控制的理解。
3.認識並綜合體內平衡的原理，即主要器官系統在生理上如何相互關聯以維持人類健康。

在學期階段，學生將廣泛瞭解身體系統如何在細胞，組織和器官系統水平上發揮作用，並能夠將簡單的生理過程聯繫起來，以更好地了解社會中高度流行的疾病和對生物醫學工程重要實用框架。

人體結構和功能的課程目標：
1.人體是一個實用的結構，它由四種主要類型的數十億個較小的結構組成：細胞，組織，器官和系統。
2.器官是幾種不同種類的組織，如此排列，以至於它們可以一起執行特殊功能。
3.系統是一個由不同數量和種類的器官組成的組織，它們如此排列，以至於它們可以一起為身體執行複雜的功能。
4.十個主要系統包括骨骼，肌肉，神經，內分泌，心血管，淋巴，呼吸，消化，泌尿和生殖系統。
5.身體功能是身體系統的生理或心理功能。身體的生存取決於身體維持或恢復其內部環境的體內平衡，這是一種相對恆定的狀態。
6.人類的生命過程包括組織、新陳代謝、反應性、運動、繁殖、生長、分化、呼吸、消化和排泄。所有這些過程在微調的平衡中協同工作，以維護個人的健康和維持生活。 
7.生命依賴於環境中的某些物理因素，包括水，氧氣，營養物質，熱量和壓力。
人體的結構和功能的課程實踐體驗 
如果人體解剖學和生理學的想法看起來很可怕，請不要擔心。本課程將通過以平易近人且相關的格式涵蓋這些主題來減輕您可能有的任何恐懼。本課程將使您對人體所有複雜的功能和系統如何協同工作更加自信，並將您從解剖學和生理學方面學到的知識與您已經瞭解的身體聯繫起來。將此視為人體使用者指南。有些人可能會說你不能沒有它！

本課程還將涵蓋身體的主要系統，並解釋它們是如何工作的，為什麼它們有時不起作用。此外，它還將檢查不同的疾病和紊亂，醫學的最新進展以及照顧身體的方法。課程包括現實生活中的例子和互動練習，讓你批判性地思考自己的經歷，並與課程建立聯繫。在整個課程中都使用全面綜合知識和理解，為您提供必要的學習材料，以便在您繼續接受教育或職業生涯時保留本課程及以後的內容。在本課程結束時，你將對人體的奇妙複雜性有更大的欣賞和理解。

description.zh: 本課程探討智慧醫療影像與生醫訊號處理技術及其在臨床應用中的分析與判讀方法。課程涵蓋醫學影像與訊號處理的基本概念，包括影像增強、雜訊抑制、濾波、邊緣偵測、影像分割與對齊等原理與技術，以及生醫訊號之前處理與特徵擷取方法。在此基礎上，進一步介紹機器學習與深度學習於醫療影像分類、偵測與分割之應用。課程同時涵蓋模型評估指標、模型統計與可解釋性分析，以及影像—文字多模態模型在輔助臨床判讀中的潛力與限制。此外亦探討資料倫理、隱私治理與主權 AI 等議題，使學生了解醫療影像模型部署於實際場域時所面臨的挑戰。
description.en: This course explores intelligent medical imaging and biomedical signal processing techniques, along with their analytical and interpretive methods in clinical applications. It covers fundamental concepts of medical image and signal processing, including the principles and techniques of image enhancement, noise suppression, filtering, edge detection, image segmentation, and registration, as well as biomedical signal preprocessing and feature extraction methods. Building upon this foundation, the course further introduces the application of machine learning and deep learning to medical image classification, detection, and segmentation. It also addresses model evaluation metrics, model statistics, interpretability analysis, and the potential and limitations of image–text multimodal models in assisting clinical interpretation. name.zh: 智慧醫療影像與訊號處理
name.en: Intelligent Medical Imaging and Signal Processing

description.zh: 本課程探討智慧醫療影像與生醫訊號處理技術及其在臨床應用中的分析與判讀方法。課程涵蓋醫學影像與訊號處理的基本概念，包括影像增強、雜訊抑制、濾波、邊緣偵測、影像分割與對齊等原理與技術，以及生醫訊號之前處理與特徵擷取方法。在此基礎上，進一步介紹機器學習與深度學習於醫療影像分類、偵測與分割之應用。課程同時涵蓋模型評估指標、模型統計與可解釋性分析，以及影像—文字多模態模型在輔助臨床判讀中的潛力與限制。此外亦探討資料倫理、隱私治理與主權 AI 等議題，使學生了解醫療影像模型部署於實際場域時所面臨的挑戰。
description.en: This course explores intelligent medical imaging and biomedical signal processing techniques, along with their analytical and interpretive methods in clinical applications. It covers fundamental concepts of medical image and signal processing, including the principles and techniques of image enhancement, noise suppression, filtering, edge detection, image segmentation, and registration, as well as biomedical signal preprocessing and feature extraction methods. Building upon this foundation, the course further introduces the application of machine learning and deep learning to medical image classification, detection, and segmentation. It also addresses model evaluation metrics, model statistics, interpretability analysis, and the potential and limitations of image–text multimodal models in assisting clinical interpretation. In addition, topics such as data ethics, privacy governance, and sovereign AI are discussed, enabling students to understand the challenges of deploying medical ima

syllabi.outline:
This course takes a modular approach to explore core research directions in modern computer vision, covering visual recognition foundations, object detection and dense prediction, vision-language and generative models, representation learning and practical challenges, and real-world vision systems. Each module spans 2–3 weeks to allow students to genuinely engage with the problem context rather than survey topics at a surface level.

The course is conducted entirely in English (EMI). Through lectures, guided paper reading, model experiments, and a final research project, students develop the ability to read papers, design experiments, and propose research directions relevant to ECE applications including edge computing, smart manufacturing, and AIoT perception.

name.en: Multimedia Service in Heterogeneous Network Environment

description.zh: 本課程介紹異質多網多媒體的特性與架構，包含：有線及無線網路的內容介紹，以及整合有線及無線網路成為異質網路的概念，其中將針對IEEE 802.21 Media Independent Handover (MIH)教導學生針對異質網路垂直切換的原理及技術。最後，對於多媒體服務技術及原理做介紹，包含：VoIP服務以及視訊串流服務的介紹，以及如何針對 多種異質網路整合多媒體服務的介紹，藉此提升學生對於新世代異質多網多媒體服務之認識。
description.en: This course introduces the characteristics and architecture of multimedia service in heterogeneous network environment. First, wired and wireless networks, e.g., 3G/3.5G/4G, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and other popular wireless access techniques, would be introduced one by one. Then, by describing the theory and technology of IEEE 802.21 Media Independent Handover (MIH), this course would show how to integrate multiple different networks into heterogeneous network environments and how to handoff among them. Finally, regarding multimedia service, VoIP and video streaming services would be taken into consideration. This course would introduce how to provide multimedia services over heterogeneous network environment. Therefore, students can learn the next-generation techniques about multimedia services in heterogeneous network environment from this course.

syllabi.outline:
本課程介紹異質多網多媒體的特性與架構，在多媒體部分，介紹多媒體基本組成、編解碼(Codec)原理、串流(Streaming)協定；在網路部分，介紹常用之有線(Ethernet)及無線網路(Wi-Fi、Bluetooth、Cellular/Mobile)，以及針對多媒體設計之網路機制，最後，配合研究所性質，透過論文導讀方式介紹當下視訊串流(Video Streaming)的最新發展，藉此提升學生對於新世代異質多網多媒體服務之認識。

1. 修課學生可從本課程學習視訊串流(Video Streaming)。
2. 修課學生可從本課程學習異質化網路(Heterogeneous Networks)。
3. 修課學生可從本課程練習相關軟體實作(Software Implementation)技巧。

syllabi.outline:
什麼是人體結構和功能？
人體結構與功能是一門非必修主要課程，旨在探索人體形式和功能之間的基本關係。解剖學和生理學是生命科學中兩個最基本的術語和研究領域。解剖學是指身體的內部和外部結構及其物理關係，而生理學是指研究這些結構的功能。本課程旨在定義瞭解剖學和生理學，並解釋了為什麼它們對生物醫學工程很重要。主要器官系統的解剖學和生理學將在正常和疾病狀態的背景下進行研究。學生將學習關鍵的生物過程，如中心教條，膜擴散和運輸，細胞信號傳導，氣體交換，血流，營養吸收，血液pH平衡以及動作電位的產生和傳播。然後，學生將應用這些知識來瞭解器官如何對維持體內平衡的各種輸入做出反應。

課程將納入實踐演示，為課程中提供的資訊提供實用框架：
1.根據位置，功能，關鍵成分和解剖命名法確定主要的人體系統。  
2.展示對代謝功能和每個主要器官系統的生理控制的理解。
3.認識並綜合體內平衡的原理，即主要器官系統在生理上如何相互關聯以維持人類健康。

在學期階段，學生將廣泛瞭解身體系統如何在細胞，組織和器官系統水平上發揮作用，並能夠將簡單的生理過程聯繫起來，以更好地了解社會中高度流行的疾病和對生物醫學工程重要實用框架。

人體結構和功能的課程目標：
1.人體是一個實用的結構，它由四種主要類型的數十億個較小的結構組成：細胞，組織，器官和系統。
2.器官是幾種不同種類的組織，如此排列，以至於它們可以一起執行特殊功能。
3.系統是一個由不同數量和種類的器官組成的組織，它們如此排列，以至於它們可以一起為身體執行複雜的功能。
4.十個主要系統包括骨骼，肌肉，神經，內分泌，心血管，淋巴，呼吸，消化，泌尿和生殖系統。
5.身體功能是身體系統的生理或心理功能。身體的生存取決於身體維持或恢復其內部環境的體內平衡，這是一種相對恆定的狀態。
6.人類的生命過程包括組織、新陳代謝、反應性、運動、繁殖、生長、分化、呼吸、消化和排泄。所有這些過程在微調的平衡中協同工作，以維護個人的健康和維持生活。 
7.生命依賴於環境中的某些物理因素，包括水，氧氣，營養物質，熱量和壓力。
人體的結構和功能的課程實踐體驗 
如果人體解剖學和生理學的想法看起來很可怕，請不要擔心。本課程將通過以平易近人且相關的格式涵蓋這些主題來減輕您可能有的任何恐懼。本課程將使您對人體所有複雜的功能和系統如何協同工作更加自信，並將您從解剖學和生理學方面學到的知識與您已經瞭解的身體聯繫起來。將此視為人體使用者指南。有些人可能會說你不能沒有它！

本課程還將涵蓋身體的主要系統，並解釋它們是如何工作的，為什麼它們有時不起作用。此外，它還將檢查不同的疾病和紊亂，醫學的最新進展以及照顧身體的方法。課程包括現實生活中的例子和互動練習，讓你批判性地思考自己的經歷，並與課程建立聯繫。在整個課程中都使用全面綜合知識和理解，為您提供必要的學習材料，以便在您繼續接受教育或職業生涯時保留本課程及以後的內容。在本課程結束時，你將對人體的奇妙複雜性有更大的欣賞和理解。

05. 轉換編碼（KLT，DFT，DCT，DST以及Walsh-Hadamard轉換）
06. 分頻編碼法（G.722 Speech coding，MPEG audio coding）
07. 小波編碼法（SPIHT，JPEG2000）

09. 跑長編碼法
10. 主題探討
description.en:
This course is mainly focused on the principles of data compression techniques as well as the state-of-the-art compression standards. The course content includes
01. Huffman codes
02. Arithmetic codes
03. Scalar quantization and Vector quantization
04. Linear prediction and Predictive coding（DPCM，ADPCM，JPEG-LS）
05. Transform coding（KLT, DFT, DCT, DST, and WHT）
06. Subband coding（G.722 Speech coding，MPEG audio coding）
07. Wavelet-Based Compression（SPIHT, JPEG2000）
08. Dictionary techniques
09. Runlength coding
10. Selected topics

description.zh: 本課程以國際時事為主軸，培養學生於英語口語互動中之理解、回應、分析與論述能力。藉由課堂討論、小組對話、議題回應、立場表述及簡短口頭報告等活動，學生將學習從多元角度理解國際事件，整理資訊、辨識觀點，並以清楚且具邏輯的英語參與討論。課程亦著重培養批判思考與國際視野，以提升學生在全球議題脈絡中之英語溝通能力。
description.en: This course centers on international current affairs and aims to develop students’ ability to comprehend, respond to, analyze, and articulate ideas in spoken English interaction. Through class discussion, small-group dialogue, issue-based responses, position statements, and short oral presentations, students will learn to approach international events from multiple perspectives, organize information, identify viewpoints, and participate in discussion in clear and logical English. The course also emphasizes the development of critical thinking and global awareness in order to strengthen students’ English communication skills in the context of global issues.

description.en: This course focuses on thematic spoken interaction and aims to develop students’ ability to engage in meaningful, structured, and sustained communication in English. Rather than emphasizing everyday conversation or formal presentation, the course trains students to express ideas, respond to others, ask follow-up questions, extend discussion, and connect viewpoints around a topic or theme. Through pair interaction, small-group discussion, topic-based response tasks, and short speaking activities, students will learn to organize ideas more clearly and participate in more coherent and extended spoken exchanges in English. The course serves as a foundation for subsequent coursework in English presentations in professional fields.

name.en: Start to APP Design and Application

description.zh:
學習相似於Microsoft Power Point 的「拖-拉-點-選」操作方式，再加上一小部份的 Low Code程式編碼，即可以設計與製作出:「專業級的 APP」 !
本課程運用學校內的雲端平台: AgilePoint NX，改變了以往撰寫APP 的模式，不再需要撰寫複雜的程式碼，讓學生專注於 APP的邏輯流程與UI(使用者介面)，進而發展貼近市場裡的商業模式，設計出精彩的APP!
課程的教學，採用傳統臺北工專的黑手工程師訓練模式:
「由經入史」:先講解理論架構，進而延伸到產業的實務運用。
嚴格要求上課同學動手實做，達成每週的設定目標。課堂上講師所示範的範例非常豐富，下課後會有一定份量的Homework(實作型作業)。
經此系統化訓練，在APP的設計與製作上，將擁有踏實的內涵與技術，增強在校學生，未來在職場上的競爭力。
「讓不懂IT(資訊工程)、非理工背景的學生，更能設計出高人氣的APP! 」
description.en: Learn the "Click and Drag" operation method, as like Microsoft Power Point, and adds some Low-Code, you can design and create: "Professional APP"!This course uses the cloud platform in the school: AgilePoint NX, which changes the mode of writing APP in the past, no longer needs to write complex code, let students focus on the logic flow of the APP and UI (user interface), and then close to the market requirement. This course uses the Taipei Tech Practical-Engineer training method:"From Theory to Practical": First explain the theoretical structure, and then extend to the practical application of the industry. Through this systematic training, in the design and production of APP, we will have practical connotation and technology to enhance the competitiveness of students in college and the future in the workplace."Let students who don't understand IT (information engineering) and non-technical backgrounds can design great and popular APPs!"

「由經入史」:先講解理論架構，進而延伸到產業的實務運用。
嚴格要求上課同學動手實做，達成每週的設定目標。課堂上講師所示範的範例非常豐富，下課後會有一定份量的Homework(實作型作業)。
經此系統化訓練，在APP的設計與製作上，將擁有踏實的內涵與技術，增強在校學生，未來在職場上的競爭力。
「讓不懂IT(資訊工程)、非理工背景的學生，更能設計出高人氣的APP! 」
Learn the "Click and Drag" operation method, as like Microsoft Power Point, and adds some Low-Code, you can design and create: "Professional APP"!This course uses the cloud platform in the school: AgilePoint NX, which changes the mode of writing APP in the past, no longer needs to write complex code, let students focus on the logic flow of the APP and UI (user interface), and then close to the market requirement. This course uses the Taipei Tech Practical-Engineer training method:"From Theory to Practical": First explain the theoretical structure, and then extend to the practical application of the industry. Through this systematic training, in the design and production of APP, we will have practical connotation and technology to enhance the competitiveness of students in college and the future in the workplace."Let students who don't understand IT (information engineering) and non-technical backgrounds can design great and popular APPs!"

description.zh:
本課程旨在教授學生如何運用創意編程和視覺化電腦圖形技術，將資料及音訊數據轉換為可視化之2D或3D視覺內容，藉以增進資料及音訊之閱聽體驗。課程進行中，學生將習得多種基於演算法之視覺表現方式，以滿足設計層面中富含躍動感、平衡感以及美感之體驗需求，活用創意編程與新媒體技術來創建更生動、更具有影響
力的動靜態視聽影像。
description.en: This course aims to teach students how to utilize the knowledge from data science and computer graphics technology to represent data and audio into visualized 2D/3D representations, which gives rise to enhanced experiences of reading and listening. Students will learn a variety of programming skills to design visual representation based on algorithms to deliver dynamic, balanced and aesthetic experiences. With the help of creative coding and new media technology, more vivid and influential static and dynamic visual and audio experiences will be generated.

description.zh: 本課程之目標在於從科學哲學層次、研究方法層次、與實際操作層次探討設計研究的本質，內容包括界定設計研究問題、選用適當的量化或質性研究方法與特定工具、研究結果詮釋、案例解析、以及論文寫作等，俾使同學具備研究之基礎觀念以及進行創作或理論論文寫作之能力。研究方法一強調研究素養及理念設計，課程內容包含研究的基本概念、文獻探討、研究問題、研究變項、研究假設、研究設計、資料蒐集與分析、研究工具、研究樣本、研究倫理與研究論文撰寫等。教學以課堂講授與論文研討與發表為主要方式，並以隨堂測驗、報告與分組討論與發表為評量依據。
description.en:
The aims of this course are to explore the nature of design research at the three various levels of scientific philosophy, research methods, and practical execution. The contents involve the introduction of defining the design problems, selecting the quantitative or qualitative research methods and specific instruments, interpretation of research results, case studies, as well as writing a thesis. This research methods one focus on research literacy and conceptual design that content details includes fundamental concept of research, literature 
review, research problem, research variables, research hypothesis, research design, data collection and analysis, research instruments, research samples, research ethics and writing up. The teaching methods include lectures, paper discussion and presentation based on the course assessment of assigned project, panel discussion and individual/group presentation.

The course aims to develop broad understanding on interaction design for students, based on theory and practice course structure. Course topics include essential factors of interactive

syllabi.outline:
Principle of Interaction Design: Autumn 2026 - Syllabus
Credit Hours: 2.0
Instructors: Ryan Sheng-Ming Wang


Course Description: 
"Interaction Design" blends theoretical and practical perspectives in the areas of visualization and interactivity into several focused aspects using interactivity for education, entertainment, interactive media design and industrial design purposes. 
An interface is the link between a user and a design that communicates how a design will be used, creating an experience for the people who will use it. It provides the framework, elements, and resources for a “conversation” to take place between users and design.
 In this course, we will explore the fundamentals of interfaces and the interaction design process. Students will be introduced to and have opportunity to practice the fundamental concepts, methods, and practices of interaction design. They will explore the ideas of "User Experience Observation ", "Form Follows Function" and "User Interaction Analysis and Evaluation". They will explore how interactive media create experiences, and understand the role that interaction with contents and installment fulfills in human existence. Finally and most importantly, students need to learn how to improve their ability to present their design ideas.
This is a class with time devoted to lecture, discussion, practice activities, design work sessions, and critique of practical work. 


Course Objectives/Goals: 
At the conclusion of the course, students will be able to: 
1.	Identify how increasingly complex technologies are integrated into designs, services and events. 
2.	Define how digital or physical artifacts behave in response to user-centric interaction. 
3.	Describe, test and evaluate the usability and sustainability of user interfaces. 
4.	Apply iterative cycles of research, testing and development based on the understanding of user needs, goals and experiences. 
5.	Develop solutions and processes to common or known interface problems. 
6.	Build and test rapid prototypes for look and feel and usability. 
7.	Utilize client based concept development to develop the strategy, information architecture, human-computer interaction and interface design. 
8.	Demonstrate competency in information architecture, human-computer interaction and interface design.

name.zh: 智慧醫療大數據實作與分析
name.en: Smart Healthcare Big Data Implementation and Analysis

description.zh: 本課程內容涵蓋次世代定序技術之基因體大數據、電子健康紀錄資料與醫電訊號實作與分析，將學習定序資料之分析流程與工具、病歷資料庫使用和訊號處理、特徵擷取與機器學習等應用。
description.en: This course covers genomic big data from next-generation sequencing technologies, electronic health record data, and biomedical signal processing and analysis. Students will learn sequencing data analysis pipelines and tools, the use of clinical databases, and applications of signal processing, feature extraction, and machine learning.

syllabi.outline:
本課程旨在介紹智慧醫療領域中常見之生醫大數據分析技術與應用，培養學生運用資訊科技解決醫療與生命科學問題之能力。課程內容涵蓋基礎生物學概念、生物資訊的經典演算法、基因體學與轉錄體學資料分析流程，以及微陣列（Microarray）、次世代定序（Next-Generation Sequencing, NGS）等高通量生物技術。學生將學習DNA定序分析、RNA定序分析及總體基因體（Metagenomics）分析方法，並透過實作熟悉生醫大數據分析流程。此外，課程邀請生醫領域專家進行專題演講，介紹電子病歷（Electronic Health Records, EHR）、基因體學（Genomics）、代謝體學（Metabolomics）等智慧醫療大數據之實務應用與發展趨勢。透過案例分析與閱讀期刊討論，培養學生整合生醫資料與人工智慧技術之能力。
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to biomedical big data analytics and its applications in smart healthcare. Topics include fundamental biological concepts, classical bioinformatics algorithms, genomic and transcriptomic data analysis, and high-throughput technologies such as Microarray and Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS). Students will learn the principles and practical workflows of DNA-seq, RNA-seq, and metagenomic analyses through hands-on exercises and real-world datasets.
The course also features invited lectures from biomedical experts covering emerging applications of healthcare big data, including Electronic Health Records (EHRs), Genomics, Metabolomics, and other multi-omics data. Through case studies, journal paper discussions, and practical projects, students will gain experience in integrating biomedical data analytics with artificial intelligence techniques to address challenges in healthcare, precision medicine, and biomedical research.

statistics through the study and practice of data analysis. Topics
include numerical and graphical summaries of data, hypothesis testing,
confidence intervals, analysis of variance, and regression. Upon
completion of this course, students should be able to think critically
about data and apply standard statistical inference procedures to draw
conclusions from such analysis.

description.zh: 本課程將涵蓋電腦科學的理論基礎。其內容包含自動機理論，電腦語言學，以及計算形式等。電腦相關的基本數學也將涵蓋在課程範圍之中。包括集合論，基本關係及及操作，以及理論證明工具與技術。課程大綱:基礎理論介紹，有限狀態自動機 / 一般敘述語法，Regular 集合的基本性質，前後文無相關文法， Pushdown 自動機，杜林機（turning machines），Chomsky 層次結構，基本關係及操作，理論證明技術及工具。
description.en: This course will look the theoretical foundation in computer science.  Automata theory, languages, and computation formalism will be examined in details.  Various fundamental computer-related mathematics will also be covered.  They include, sets/subsets, basic relations and operations and tools/techniques for proving theorems. Course Outline: Introduction to Theoretical Foundations, Finite Automata / Regular Expression, Properties of Regular Sets, Context-Free Grammars, Pushdown Automata, Turing Machines, The Chomsky Hierarchy (tentative), Basic Relations and Operations, Tools/Techniques for Proving Theorems.

description.zh: 嵌入式系統目前愈來愈普遍。它將會大大地影響我們的生活方式。可攜式裝置如智慧型手機、掌上型電腦、以及所謂的IA裝置如家用網路閘道器、數位視訊錄影機、和常見的遊戲機都是屬於嵌入式系統的範疇。在本課程中,我們將會討論何謂嵌入式系統、嵌入式系統的形式、以及如何建構一個嵌入式系統。由於嵌入式系統包含硬體及軟體的議題，我們也會探討相關的主題。 本課程的先修課程包含計算機組織與結構、C程式語言、資料結構、系統程式、以及作業系統。課程主要內容如下：嵌入式系統簡介與概論、嵌入式精簡指令集結構、ARM指令集、嵌入式計算平台、嵌入式程式設計與分析、嵌入式作業系統、系統設計技術、裝置操作、網路。本課程亦包含實習與學期專題作業。
description.en: Embedded systems are more and more popular today. It will affect the human life greatly. Portable devices like smart phone, PDA, and MP3 player, and so-called IA devices such as home gateway, DVR, and game machine are all categorized as embedded systems. In this course, we will discuss what an embedded system is, what it looks like, and how to build an embedded device. Since an embedded system involves hardware and software issues, we will discuss the related subjects. The prerequisite courses for this class include computer organization and architecture, the C programming language, data structure, system programming, and operating system. The major topics of this course are listed as follows: Introduction and Basic Concepts, The RISC Embedded Architectures, The ARM instruction Set, The Embedded Computing Platforms, Program Design and Analysis, The Embedded Operating Systems, System Design Techniques, Device Manipulation, Networks.

syllabi.outline:
An embedded system is a computing system designed for a specific function or set of tasks and integrated into a device or product. 
1. Design and implement a basic communication protocol (packet format, length, checksums, error handling, and retransmission strategy).
2. Use an RTOS (such as FreeRTOS or Zephyr) to establish multitasking, synchronization (Semaphore, Queue, Mutex), and time management.
3. Create a userspace program + systemd service + simple network communication (Socket, MQTT, HTTP) on an Embedded Linux platform.
4. Write modular firmware/system services on an MCU or Linux platform, implementing GPIO, timers, UART, I2C, SPI, ADC, and PWM.

description.zh: 本課程介紹電腦科學中圖形識別的基本原理與相關技術，使學生了解各種圖形識別的分類方法，經由對分類問題的分析，瞭解如何將輸入樣本依不同特性加以分類，並熟悉圖形識別系統之相關議題如：分割、特徵擷取、分類、後處理、訓練、監督/非監督式學習、機器學習，進而了解分類問題，增進其解決實際圖形識別分類問題的能力。課程內容包括下列課題：圖形識別概論, Bayesian Decision Theory, Maximum-Likelihood, 非參數法學習, K-Nearest Neighbor Estimation, The Nearest-Neighbor Rule, Positive Boolean Function多分類器, Linear Discriminant Functions，高維資料分類, 分類正確率評估(Accuracy Assessments)及其他重要的應用，例如: 文件分析、生物辨識、影像監控、遙測影像分類、醫療診斷、資料探勘等概念，最後並透過相關論文的研讀及討論，了解近代圖形識別的最新發展趨勢。

name.en: Special Topics on Nano- Technology and Environment

description.zh: 這門課著重在探討奈米科技之基本原理與應用範疇，以及環境應用與安全相關主題，內容包含奈米之基本特性、各種量測方法、結構控制、以及"納米"對環境應用與安全問題。此外並包含奈米微粒之產生、收集、測量以及微粒動力學等主題。
description.en: This course will investigate the definition and theories of nanotechnology. Including basic properties, measuring methods, structural control, environmental, and safety issues of "Nano-". Topics about generation, collection, measurement and dynamics of nano-particle will also be covered.

syllabi.outline: This course introduces students to the environmental aspects of nanoscience and nanotechnology. In this course, students will learn the fundamental physical-chemical properties, synthesis and characterization, environmental implications, health and environmental impact, and environmental applications of nanoparticles and nanomaterials. Topics about the nanomaterial applications in low/zero-carbon emission will also be covered. Case studies from recent publications on engineered carbon nanomaterials and nanomaterials on catalysis will be discussed.

name.zh: 全民國防教育-防衛動員

description.zh: 「全民國防教育法」自民國95年2月開始施行，以國際情勢、國防政策、全民國防、防衛動員、國防科技五大主軸作為全民國防教育的課程規畫。「防衛動員」單元，在探討全民防衛動員的意義與功能，說明全民防衛動員對國家安全的重要性；並介紹青年服勤動員內涵，讓學生體會自己在全民防衛動員體系中所扮演的角色，進而涵養愛國意識，深化全民國防共識。
description.en: In order to meet the requirement of Act of All-Out Defense Education that put into action in February 2006, the curriculum of All-Out Defense Education Military Training planned by Ministry of Education is divided into five sections: International Situations, National Defense Policies, Civil Defense, Defense Mobilization, and Military Technology.The 'Defense Mobilization' unit explores the meaning and functions of nationwide defense mobilization, emphasizing its importance to national security. It also introduces the concept of youth service mobilization, helping students understand the role they play within the national defense mobilization system. Through this, students cultivate a sense of patriotism and deepen the collective consensus on national defense.

name.zh: 全民國防教育-防衛動員

description.zh: 「全民國防教育法」自民國95年2月開始施行，以國際情勢、國防政策、全民國防、防衛動員、國防科技五大主軸作為全民國防教育的課程規畫。「防衛動員」單元，在探討全民防衛動員的意義與功能，說明全民防衛動員對國家安全的重要性；並介紹青年服勤動員內涵，讓學生體會自己在全民防衛動員體系中所扮演的角色，進而涵養愛國意識，深化全民國防共識。
description.en: In order to meet the requirement of Act of All-Out Defense Education that put into action in February 2006, the curriculum of All-Out Defense Education Military Training planned by Ministry of Education is divided into five sections: International Situations, National Defense Policies, Civil Defense, Defense Mobilization, and Military Technology.The 'Defense Mobilization' unit explores the meaning and functions of nationwide defense mobilization, emphasizing its importance to national security. It also introduces the concept of youth service mobilization, helping students understand the role they play within the national defense mobilization system. Through this, students cultivate a sense of patriotism and deepen the collective consensus on national defense.

syllabi.outline:
「全民國防教育法」自民國95年2月開始施行，以國際情勢、國防政策、全民國防、防衛動員、國防科技五大主軸作為全民國防教育的課程規畫。「國際情勢」單元，主要論述區域安全與兩岸情勢發展，培育學生宏觀的國際視野；更進一步說明在全球化浪潮下，國際重要的安全議題及我國的因應之道。「國防政策」單元，在論述我國國防政策內涵及大陸政策的發展，使學生認識當前國防政策施政方針，增進國防安全知識；並介紹我國國家安全法制與危機管理機制，藉此體認國家安全的重要性，加強全民國防意識。「全民國防」單元，主要論述國家意識及全民防衛的概念、內涵與重要性，並介紹國防與經濟、文化、心理的關聯，讓學生理解國防事務其實與生活息息相關，加強全民國防意識，增進對國家的認同。「防衛動員」單元，在探討全民防衛動員的意義與功能，說明全民防衛動員對國家安全的重要性；並介紹青年服勤動員內涵，讓學生體會自己在全民防衛動員體系中所扮演的角色，進而涵養愛國意識，深化全民國防共識。「國防科技」單元，主要使學生了解武器系統概況，並認識國防科技發展與我國國防產業現況，引發對國防科技的興趣，進而認同國防、支持國防。
In order to meet the requirement of Act of All-Out Defense Education that put into action in February 2006, the curriculum of All-Out Defense Education Military Training planned by Ministry of Education is divided into five sections: International Situations, National Defense Policies, Civil Defense, Defense Mobilization, and Military Technology. In International Situations, the object is to cultivate students’ broader international perspectives through discussing Asian-Pacific regional security and the development of cross-strait relation. In Civil Defense, the object is to make students aware that national defense affairs are closely related to their daily life. In Defense Mobilization, the object is to let students recognize their roles in all-out defense mobilization system. In Defense Technology, the main object is to let students overview the development of weapon systems, and understand the current development of the nation’s defense technology and defense industry.

description.zh: 研究生在第一年必須選定指導教授，以決定設計創作或論文寫作的方向，從事設計創作的研究生必須發展創作理念、創作過程與實作說明，最後彙整創作報告形同於研究論文；從事論文寫作的研究生針對互動媒體設計的相關主題進行研究，並將研究成果撰寫成為論文，其內容包含緒論、文獻探討、研究設計與實施、研究結果與討論、結論與建議等。本課程目的旨在培養獨立企劃研究能力，建構研究設計與研究寫作的能力，對設計創作組而言，過程中培養協同合作的能力是必須具備的要項。
description.en: In the first year graduate students are requested to determine design creation and research topic under the supervision of their advisor. Graduate students who are chosen the fields of design creation should be developed creation principle, design process and pr92tical work. The results of design creation are considered as research thesis. Graduate students who are focus on the research of inter92tive media design should be undertaken the results of research as a thesis. The content of thesis includes introduction, literature review, research design and appro92hes, results and discussion, conclusion and suggestions. The aims of this course are to provide students with opportunity to initiate personal research into industrial design related topic. The course includes a training of developing research, writing up and references. To design creation groups. The collaborative capability is in need of the cultivation of ability during the process.

description.en: Introduction to the finite element method and its application to engineering problems.  Topics include Variational Formulation and Finite Element Formulations, 1-D, 2-D and 3-D Element Shapes, Numerical Integration, Applications to dynamic problem and Introduction to Commercial Finite Element Programs.

syllabi.outline:
Course Title: Finite Element Analysis (有限元素分析)
This course introduces the basic principles of the finite element method and its applications in various engineering problems. Topics include fundamental concepts of finite element analysis, establishing finite element models using variational principles, shape functions, and iso-parametric elements. It covers one-dimensional problems such as rods, trusses, beams, and frames; two-dimensional problems including plane stress, plane strain, and plate-shell problems; and three-dimensional problems involving general solids. Practical exercises and case studies using finite element analysis software are included for practice and research analysis.
The course is based on 16 + 2 weeks of flexible learning.

description.zh: 課程內容包括：課程分為三部分，第一、接合技術之基礎：材料表面結構和接合力學。第二、介紹一般工程用接合技術：機械接合、銲接、銲接冶金、軟硬銲、金屬-陶瓷接合、擴散鍵結、和膠合。第三、接合應用：真空系統和微電子接合和密封結構介紹。
description.en: This course is divided into three sections. The first three chapters deal with those chapters which are the principles of joining, including: Introduction, Surface science, and The mechanics of joining. The next six chapters describe the engineering options currently available for the joining and assembly of the components of an engineering system, including: Mechanical bonding, Welding, Welding Metallurgy, Soldering & Brazing, Metal-Ceramic Joints & Diffusion Bonding, Adhesives, and Structural Adhesives. The last two chapters take two areas of special interest, vacuum system and microelectronics, and survey the range of resolutions to joining problems which have been developed for these specific application.

description.zh:
本課程主要在教導學生探討基本室內環境品質與人體健康間的關係，使學生具備創造健康室內環境的相關知識及操作能力，主要授課要點如下：
1.以各種類型的建築室內環境為主題；
2.探討人為環境與人體健康之關係；
3.探討建築材料、構造與設備對室內環境各項因子之影響；
4.學習室內環境品質量測儀器之操作與判讀能力；
5.具備診斷與改善一般室內環境議題之相關專業知識及操作能力。
description.en:
The purpose of this course is to discuss the relationship between Indoor Environment Quality and human healthy, and make sure our students can realize the knowledge of healthy environment and manage it.
Contents：

2. The relationship between the artificial environment and human health.
3. Discuss the influence of the building material, construction and equipment on indoor environment.
4. Learn to use the instrument to measure indoor environment quality.
5. Learn to diagnose and improve indoor environment quality.

syllabi.outline: 為追求「永續發展與人本健康」之目的，使既有與新建的居住環境，配合我國「室內空氣品質管理法」規範下運作，提昇民眾居住環境健康品質效益，針對病態建築之環境問題，其涵蓋醫療、法律、建築、化學、生物等領域，綜合診斷以進行改善。本課程為第一階段之系列課程，其內容包括： 一.健康環境概念：說明何謂「病態建築」，探討室內空氣與健康之關係。 二.建築物污染源：探討來自各建築材料的化學物質逸散及其對人體健康之影響，並提出室內污染物質濃度減低對策。 三.生物性污染源：探討黴菌、蹣、白蟻及寵物等帶來的室內空氣污染。 四.診斷技術：說明室內空氣品質診斷方法及病態建築改善之專業技術，配合案例介紹探討新、舊建築物室內環境品質的設計預防、診斷改善技術。

description.zh: 當 Lumiere 兄弟於 1895 年末在巴黎一家咖啡館,舉辦第一場售票的電影放映會時,也正是全球第二次工業革命如火如荼影響人們的生產方式與都市生活之際,透過紀錄當代都市活動與工業化機械美學的短片,他們讓電影技術與城市發展從最初就密不可分,共同作為歌頌現代性的重要媒介。然而,學術界要遲到約莫百年之後,從 1990 年代開始才逐漸形成專門探討電影與城市互動關係的跨學門領域。來自電影研究、都市研究、地理學、歷史學、比較文學、區域研究??等等領域的學者們,於過去三十數年間替電影城市研究貢獻心力。他們不只是藉由電影分析與相關史料爬梳來重新理解現代性、現代主義與當代都市的發展,也同時關注於二次大戰後流行的黑色電影(film noir)如何將當時的都市議題作為其創作主題,後續於 1970 年代起流行的各種近未來反烏托邦電影,又是怎麼進一步藉由預測人類都市的發展來反思當下,創造電影與城市間更為複雜的互文關係。千禧年之後,隨著電影工業與市場的全球化,電影逐漸成為具有都市行銷潛力的大眾媒體,電影場景更逐步發展成一個重要的觀光類型。同時因為電影技術門檻降低與社群媒體的發展,電影也不再只是電影公司或具有天份的獨立電影工作者的遊戲,更多難以分類的影像對都市空間進
description.en: While cinema has been invented over a hundred years and getting influential in shaping people’s perspectives to our environments, the studies of cinematic urbanism have only initiated since 1990s. During the past decades, this interdisciplinary field has developed upon the scholarships of various disciplines, including film and media studies, cultural studies, history, geography, urban studies, etc. This course intends to introduce this still young field through chronologically examining the relationships between cinema and cities, from both being used to celebrate and mediate the modern feelings,to film noir playing a crucial role to criticize and depict urban problems, and to cinematic urban imaginaries boosting tourism and intervening in urban process. Students will learn the theories and methodologies of cinematic urbanism studies, comprehending cinema and different urban spaces as powerful medium that could be manipulated to create, transmit, and perceive certain ideologies.

description.zh:
資訊都市主義（informatical urbanism或informational urbanism）為一跨領域學科，旨在透過資訊環境與流程之輔助，推動政策、規劃、發展、策略行動、設計之都市與社區進程。
本課程主要在協助學生，以都市與社區問題為基本導向，建立資訊環境與流程之規劃能力。
授課主要涵蓋面向：1.資訊與知識基礎設施 2.經濟面向 3.都市治理與公共行政 4.都市空間之資訊化 5.地點因子 6.使用者行為 7.特殊議題。
description.en:
Informatical urbanism (or informational urbanism) is an interdisciplinary area of knowledge, and it mainly utilize the facilitation of informatical environments and procedures for the progression of policy, planning, development, strategic initiative, and design within cities and communities.
During this course, student will acquire the planning capability of establish such applicable informatical environments and procedures, based upon explorations of urban and community issues.
Main contents of this course: 1. Information and knowledge infrastructures, 2. Economic aspects, 3. Urban governance and administration, 4. Informaticalization of urban space, 5. Location factors, 6. User behavior, 7. Focus area of problem.

name.en: Interactive Installation and Performing Arts Technology

description.zh: 本課程介紹整合即時影像、即時音訊、實體裝置、及相關表演科技（如燈光控制、各類感應器應用等）之技術與應用實務，並藉由圖形化、物件導向程式設計系統，引導未有程式設計經驗的視覺設計者或輔助已有程式設計能力者，以更有效率的方式進行相關互動系統設計，藉以達成互動裝置、表演科技、與表演藝術之整合。
description.en: This course introduces the technology that help integrates real-time video, audio, installations, and associated performance arts technology (such as lighting control, the application of various types of sensors, etc.) into performing arts. Through a graphical, object-oriented programming system, the course is intended to help visual designers with no programming experiences or to assist experienced programmers to efficiently design the interactive systems that combine interactive installations, performance arts technology, and performing arts itself as a whole.

syllabi.outline:
This course will explore the possibilities and developments of using interactive technology in contemporary performing arts and installation design. It will introduce forms and aesthetics of interactive performance, computer vision and listening, real-time video processing, and real-time audio synthesis. Through proposing and executing actual performance projects and interdisciplinary collaboration, students will have the opportunity to integrate interactive technology, interactive installations, and performing arts. The course will emphasize project proposal and conceptualization, performance scripting, stage and interactive installation design, and interactive audio-visual application design.

本課程將探討互動科技運用於當代表演藝術、裝置設計之可能性與相關發展，並介紹互動表演形式與美學、電腦視覺與電腦聆聽、即時影像處理、即時音訊合成等，藉由實際展演計畫之提案與執行，透過跨領域合作，讓學生有機會將互動科技、互動裝置、表演藝術三者結合。本課程將注重展演計畫之提案與發想、表演之腳本安排、舞台與互動裝置設計、互動影音應用設計等。

name.en: Special Topics on Living Environment Design

description.zh: 本課程之目標在於研討生活環境設計之相關研究專題，以文獻研讀、論文研讀討論以及個案研究為重點，藉由密集討論、書面報告以及設計專題之之研究與實作，學生可以有效率地交換意見，獲得更深入而廣泛的體驗，並具備研究、分析、實作之能力。本所結合設計、藝術、人文、木工等各領域的學生，整合培育創新設計專業人才，因此，本課程之另一主要學習目標為建構一多元領域交互學習的環境，以專題導向式為學習模式，可分別組合具各種專長的研究生，協同完成生活環境設計專題的研究，或是透過生活環境設計個案研討、生活環境設計專題創作的方式進行。教學將以課堂講授、論文研討與發表以及專題實作為主，並以報告、分組討論與發表以及實作作品為評量方式。
description.en: The objective of this course is to discuss research topics related to living environment design, focusing on literature study, thesis study and discussion and case studies, through intensive discussion, written report and research and practice of design topics, students can exchange opinions efficiently, gain more in-depth and extensive experience, and have the ability to research, analyze and practice. Therefore, another major learning objective of this course is to construct a multi-field interactive learning environment, which can be combined with graduate students with various specialties to collaborate on research on living environment design topics, or through case studies on living environment design. Teaching will focus on classroom lectures, thesis discussions and presentations, and thematic facts, and will be evaluated by reports, group discussions and presentations, and practical works.
